AcceptInvitationRequest.description:
The invitation code from the invitation link, and the name of a person who is not a user yet, within the API's limit. The API
trims the name before it counts its length. A known user sends none.

AuditActorResponse.description:
Who acted: a user, by user id, or the platform, that is a system admin seen from a tenant's log. `displayName` is a
user's real name, or null: for a user without a name, a deleted user, an unknown user, and for the platform, which
the screen names from `kind` in its own language. `deleted` is set for a user only.

AuditActorResponseKind.description: The kind of actor of an audit entry.

AuditDetailsResponse.description:
The details of an audit entry: one shape for each operation that keeps some. `operation` names the shape, so a client narrows
`details` by it. It is the entry's own operation.

AuditEntitlementValueResponse.description:
One key's value as an entry keeps it: a feature's state in `enabled`, or a limit's number in `maximum`, or an unlimited
limit with `unlimited` true.

AuditEntryResponse.description:
One entry of an audit log: when, the operation (`member.invited`), who acted, what it was done to, and the details the entry
keeps: the shape of its operation, or null for an operation without details. Names are resolved when the log is read; a name is only
a person's real name. It holds no email address.

AuditOperation.description: The operation of an audit entry, area.action.

AuditPlanResponse.description:
A plan in the details of an audit entry, as the entry keeps it from that moment: its id and its name. The plan may be renamed since,
so the entry is its own record of it, and Audit answers it in a shape of its own, as AuditRoleResponse.

AuditRetentionResponse.description:
The tenant's Activity log period, in days, null for no limit, and the shortening that the Banner shows: null unless a hold runs and an
entry it keeps is older than the period.

AuditRetentionShorteningResponse.description: The period of a running hold, in days, and the moment the entries older than it go, at the hold's end.

AuditRoleResponse.description:
A role in the details of an audit entry, as the entry keeps it from that moment: its id, its name and whether it is built in. The
role may be gone or renamed since, so the entry is its own record of it (K3), and Audit answers it in a shape of its own (the
maintainer's decision in step r4b).

AuditTargetResponse.description:
What the action was done to: a tenant or a role with its name at that moment, a user with their real name now or null, or an
invitation, which has no name. `deleted` is set for a user only. `email` is an invitation's address now, read from the
invitation; null for any other target, for an invitation whose address a user's deletion erased (K3, A8), and in the tenant's log
for a caller without `tenant.invitations.read`.

AuditTargetResponseKind.description: The kind of target of an audit entry.

ChangeEmailRequest.description: The six digits that went to the new address.

ChangeMemberRoleRequest.description:
The id of the tenant's role to give the member. The role is required: a request without one is refused, so it never falls back to
an empty id.

ChangePreferencesRequest.description:
The user's language, one of the list, and the IANA name of their time zone, such as `Europe/Dublin`, or null for "not set":
the web then uses the browser's. Both are required, so a client that leaves the time zone out never clears it by mistake.

ChangeTenantPlanRequest.description: The plan the tenant is put on, or, in a preview, would be.

ConfirmAccountDeletionRequest.description: The six digits that went to the person's address.

CreatePlanRequest.description:
A new plan: its name, whether it takes the default mark, and its value of some keys of the list; a key left out has no value, and is
closed. The API trims the name before it counts its length.

CreateRoleRequest.description: The name of the custom role, and the names of its permissions, from the tenant pool.

CreateTenantRequest.description:
A new tenant, the email address of its first owner, who is invited once the tenant is ready, and the language of the owner's
invitation email: without one, the system admin's own. The plan the tenant goes on: without one, the default plan. The API trims the
name before it counts its length.

DataExportResponse.description:
The person's latest data export: where it is, when they asked, when it was ready, and until when they can download it, which stays after
it expired, so the screen says when the file was deleted.

DataExportResponseStatus.description:
Where a data export is: being prepared, ready to download until its expiry, failed, so the person can ask again, or expired, its file
deleted.

DownloadLinkResponse.description: A link that downloads the person's export, and when it stops working. The link is made for this answer and never stored.

EntitlementOverrideResponse.description:
A tenant's override of one key: its value, its expiry (null for one that never expires), its state, the system admin's reason, the
system admin who set it, by id and by name, and when.

EntitlementOverrideResponseState.description:
The state of an override at the moment of the request: active, or expired, when its expiry has passed. An expired override applies no
more, and stays until a system admin removes it.

EntitlementValueRequest.description:
One key's value in a request: a feature's state in `enabled`, or a limit's number of 0 or more in `maximum`, or an unlimited
limit with `unlimited` true. Exactly one, of the key's kind; else 400 `plan.entitlement_invalid` with the key. Unlimited is a
value of its own, never a number.

EntitlementValueResponse.description:
One key's value: a feature's state in `enabled`, or a limit's number in `maximum`, or an unlimited limit with
`unlimited` true. The fields of the other kind are null.

ErrorCode.description: The error's code, area.reason. A client shows its own text for it, never the English detail.

ExcessResponse.description:
One key a change would put a tenant over: what the tenant has that the key counts (`count`), the new effective value, and how far
over it goes (`amount`): the count less a limit, or the whole count for a feature that turns off while the tenant uses it.

FeatureKey.description: A feature key of the entitlement list: on or off.

FieldErrorCode.description: Why one field of a request failed validation.

GetInvitationPreviewRequest.description: The invitation code from the invitation link.

GetPlanUpdatePreviewRequest.description: The values a plan edit would give the plan, exactly as UpdatePlanRequest gives them.

InvitationPreviewResponse.description:
What the accept screen shows the invited person before they accept: the tenant's name, who invited, the role the invitation
gives (null for a finished invitation whose custom role was deleted), when it expires, and its state at the moment of the request: `pending`, `expired`, `accepted` or
`cancelled`. Only a caller with the invited address gets it.

InvitationResponse.description:
A pending invitation: the invited address, its role, the user id of the member who invited and their names as they are
stored now, when it was created and expires, and its state at the moment of the request: `pending`, or `expired` once
its expiry has passed. It is never `accepted` or `cancelled`, because the list holds pending invitations
only, and inviting answers the new one. It carries the language the invitation keeps for its email (K8), so a client that invites the
same person again can send it back.

InvitationResponseState.description:
The state of an invitation at the moment of the request: pending, expired (pending past its expiry), accepted (used) or cancelled
(revoked, replaced, or cancelled with its tenant). Every response that holds the state of an invitation uses this one enum, and says
which of its values it can hold.

InviteMemberRequest.description:
The address to invite, the id of the tenant's role the invitation gives, and the language of the invitation's email: without one,
the inviter's own. The role is required: a request without one is refused, so it never falls back to an empty id.

InviteOwnerRequest.description:
The address of the Owner the platform invites into a tenant without one, and the language of the invitation's email: without one, the
system admin's own.

InviterNameResponse.description:
Who invited: a user, with the name stored now and `deleted` for a user a system admin deleted, or the platform,
with no name and no `deleted`. The screen names the platform from `kind`, as the audit logs do.

InviterNameResponseKind.description: Who invited: a user of the tenant, or the platform, for which a system admin acted.

Language.description: A language the web speaks, by its BCP 47 language tag.

LimitKey.description: A limit key of the entitlement list: a number of 0 or more, or unlimited.

MakeOwnerRequest.description:
The id of the user to make an Owner, a member of the tenant, as the user's detail lists the user's memberships. It is required: a
request without one is refused, so it never falls back to an empty id.

MemberInvitedDetailsResponse.description: The details of `member.invited`: the role the invitation gives, and the pending invitation it replaced, if any.

MemberLeftDetailsResponse.description: The details of `member.left`: the role the member had.

MemberRemovedDetailsResponse.description: The details of `member.removed`: the role the member had.

MemberResponse.description:
A member of the tenant: the user's id, the copy of their email address and name, their role, whether the identity provider deleted
the user, and when they joined the tenant. A deleted user has an empty email address and an empty name, and
the screen shows "Deleted user", as the audit logs say `deleted` (K3).

MemberRoleChangedDetailsResponse.description: The details of `member.role_changed`: the member's old and new role.

MeResponse.description:
The signed-in user: our user id, not the identity provider's, the copy of their profile, whether they are a system admin, and
their preferences. It has no status: a suspended user is refused on every me endpoint (A9), and a deleted user cannot sign in.

additionalProperties.description: A feature's state, a limit's number, or null for an unlimited limit.

MyTenantDetailResponse.description:
The tenant of the route, for one of its members: as an item of their tenant list, with when it was created and the names of the
permissions the member's role holds there, in ordinal order. The web shows an action only when the list holds its permission; every
endpoint still checks the permission itself. It also holds the name of the tenant's plan; `entitlements`, every key of the list
with its effective value at the moment of the request, by key, as the permissions: a feature true or false, a limit a number, and null
for an unlimited limit; and `usage`, the tenant's count of each limit, so the web adds no list up. Every endpoint still checks
its feature and its limit itself.

MyTenantResponse.description:
A tenant the signed-in user belongs to: an item of their tenant list, and the tenant an invitation made them join. Its status is
active, or suspended, closed or purging when its members cannot enter it. The role is the user's there.

MyTenantResponseStatus.description: The status of a tenant as its members see it: active, or suspended, closed or purging when they cannot enter it. A purged tenant has no member.

NotificationLinkResponse.description: Where a notification leads: a kind, and the tenant it is about, none for a personal notification.

NotificationLinkResponseKind.description: Where a notification leads, which the web turns into a URL.

id.description: The notification's id, which opening it names.

title.description: The title, in the reader's language.

body.description: The body, in the reader's language.

area.description: The area it belongs to, such as "Members", in the reader's language. A label only.

actorName.description: The person who acted, named now: "Deleted user" in the reader's language for a deleted one; none when the platform acted.

tenantName.description: The organisation's name as it was at that moment; none for a notification about no organisation.

createdAt.description: When the event it tells of happened.

readAt.description: When the reader opened it; none while it is unread.

unread.description: Whether the reader has not opened it yet, from ReadAt; the filter unread compares with it.

NotificationResponse.description:
A notification as a bell shows it (U7). Its title and body are rendered in the reader's language (U2). The link names where it leads, as a
kind and the tenant it is about: the web builds the URL.

NotificationType.description: The type of a notification, area.event.

OwnerInvitationResponse.description:
The latest Owner invitation of a tenant that has no Owner: its address, its expiry, and its state at the moment of the request:
`pending`, `expired` once its expiry has passed, or `cancelled`. It is never `accepted`, because it is shown only
while the tenant has no Owner. It carries the language the invitation keeps for its email (K8), so a client that invites the Owner
again can send it back, and when it was sent, null for an invitation the API summarised before it kept the moment.

Permission.description: A name of the permission list. Every endpoint checks its own permission.

PlanListItemResponse.description: A plan in the platform's list: its name, whether it is the default plan, and how many tenants are on it.

PlanNameResponse.description: A plan as another resource names it: its id and its name.

PlanResponse.description:
A plan: its name, whether it is the default plan, how many tenants are on it, its value of each key it has one for, and when it was
created. A key the plan has no value for is closed.

PlanRetentionShortenedResponse.description:
A plan edit that makes the plan's Activity log period shorter: how many organisations on the plan it shortens, those without an
override of the key that has not expired, and the plan's period before, in days, null for no limit, and after.

PlanUpdatePreviewPageResponse.description:
A page of the tenants a plan edit would put over, in the list contract, and a shorter Activity log period, null when the edit keeps it
as long or longer. The period's count is the edit's whole, which no search or page changes.

PlatformAuditRetentionResponse.description: How long the platform's log keeps an entry, in days: the deployment setting, never unlimited.

PreferencesResponse.description: The user's preferences, which follow them to every tenant and device. A null time zone is not set.

errors.description: The field codes for each field of a request that failed validation, by the field's JSON name.

traceId.description: The trace id of the request, for the logs.

tenantIds.description: The tenants the error is about, when a client needs them to act, such as the tenants a user is the last Owner of.

entitlement.description: The entitlement key the error is about: the feature that is off, or the limit that is reached.

RenameMeRequest.description:
The signed-in user's own name, within the API's limit. The API trims the name before it counts its length. It is required, so a
client that leaves it out never clears it.

RenameTenantRequest.description: A tenant's new name. The API trims it before it counts its length. The slug never changes.

RenameUserRequest.description: A user's new name, within the API's limit. The API trims the name before it counts its length.

RequestEmailChangeRequest.description: The new address, to which the API sends a code.

ReservedSlug.description: A slug that no tenant may take, because the tenant web has or may add a route of that name.

RetentionShortenedResponse.description:
A change that makes the tenant's Activity log period shorter: the period before, in days, null for no limit, and the new one. The
entries older than the new period stay 30 days, then go.

RoleCreatedDetailsResponse.description: The details of `role.created`: the names of the new role's permissions, in ordinal order.

RoleDetailResponse.description:
A role of the tenant as the role endpoints answer it: what RoleResponse holds, the names of the role's permissions, in
ordinal order, and how many members have the role and how many pending invitations give it, an expired one included. DeleteRole
refuses a role while either count is above zero (role.in_use).

RoleResponse.description:
A role as a member, an invitation or a tenant of the signed-in user holds it: its id, its name and whether it is built in. A built-in
role answers its stored name, `owner`, `admin` or `member`; a custom role answers the name the tenant gave it (A2, A3).
A request gives a role by its id.

RoleUpdatedDetailsResponse.description: The details of `role.updated`: the old and the new name, and the permissions the change added and removed, in ordinal order.

SetEntitlementOverrideRequest.description:
The tenant's value of the key in the route, over its plan's value; its expiry, after now, or null for one that never expires; and the
system admin's reason, required. The API trims the reason before it counts its length.

SuspendTenantRequest.description:
Why the system admin suspends the tenant, within the API's limit. The API trims the reason before it counts its length. A member
never sees it. It holds no personal data, such as a person's name or email address: the platform's audit log keeps it after the
tenant's purge (A8).

SuspendUserRequest.description:
Why the system admin suspends the user, within the API's limit. The API trims the reason before it counts its length. The user never
sees it. It is personal data about the user: the user's data export holds it, the deletion erases it, and no audit entry keeps it.

TenantDetailResponse.description:
One tenant for the platform's detail screen: as an item of the list, with every Owner, in the order they joined, in place of the
first. A closed tenant says until when it can be reopened; a closed tenant, or one whose purge has begun, says when its Owners are, or
were, warned of the purge (null otherwise). It counts the pending invitations that have not expired at the moment of the request, and
names who created, suspended and closed it, as they are named now, when it was suspended and when its purge started: each null for a
seed, for an event the tenant is not in, and for an event before the API kept it.

TenantEntitlementResponse.description:
One key of a tenant's entitlements: whether it is a feature, the plan's value (null when the plan has none: the key is then closed),
the tenant's override (null when it has none), the effective value at the moment of the request, and what the tenant has that the key
counts (`count`).

TenantExcessResponse.description:
A tenant that a plan edit would put over: its id, name and slug, how far over its furthest key it goes, each such key, and the keys
that an override of the tenant still holds, which the edit does not touch.

TenantListItemResponse.description:
A tenant in the platform's list: as TenantResponse, with its plan, when it was created, until when a closed tenant can be
reopened, its members and Owners counted, its pending invitations that have not expired at the moment of the request, as the seats count
them, and, while it has no Owner, its latest Owner invitation. Each is null when it does not apply.
A purged tenant counts no member and no Owner: its purge deleted its summary with its members (K4). Its tombstone keeps when it was
created.

TenantListPageResponse.description: A page of the tenant list (K5), and how many tenants of the whole list are in each status.

TenantOwnerInvitedDetailsResponse.description:
The details of `tenant.owner_invited`: the invitation's id, the pending invitation it replaced, if any, and the invitation's address
now, read from the invitation; null when a user's deletion erased it (K3, A8), and in the tenant's log for a caller without
`tenant.invitations.read`.

TenantOwnerMadeDetailsResponse.description:
The details of `tenant.owner_made`: the member who became an Owner, and the role they had. The entry keeps the member by id only
(K3); `displayName` and `deleted` name them now, as an actor is named: `displayName` is the real name, or null for a
user without a name, a deleted user and an unknown user, and `deleted` is true for a deleted user.

TenantOwnerResponse.description: An Owner of a tenant: the user's id, name and address.

TenantPlanChangePreviewResponse.description:
What a change of the tenant's plan would put it over: each key with the count and the new value, empty when it stays within every
key, and the keys an override of the tenant still holds, which the change does not touch. A shorter Activity log period, null when the
new plan keeps it as long or longer.

TenantPlanResponse.description: A tenant's plan and every key of the list with its plan value, override, effective value and count.

TenantPurgeWarnedDetailsResponse.description: The details of `tenant.purge_warned`: the moment of the purge that the Owners were warned of.

TenantRenamedDetailsResponse.description: The details of `tenant.renamed`: the tenant's old and new name.

TenantResponse.description:
A tenant and its status, with the reason of its suspension while it is suspended, or closed after a suspension, the moment of its
closure while it is closed or purging, and the moment of its purge once it is purged. Only a system admin sees this shape.

TenantResponseStatus.description: The status of a tenant: active from its creation, suspended, closed, purging once its purge has started, or purged (K4).

TenantStatusCountsResponse.description: How many tenants are in each status, without the search or the status filter: the tabs of the Organisations list.

TenantSuspendedDetailsResponse.description: The details of `tenant.suspended`: the system admin's reason. Only the platform's log holds it.

UnreadNotificationCountResponse.description: How many notifications of a bell the reader has not opened.

UpdatePlanRequest.description:
A plan's name, its default mark and exactly these values: a key left out loses its value. The default plan keeps its mark until another
plan takes it. The API trims the name before it counts its length.

UpdateRoleRequest.description: The name the custom role takes, and exactly the permissions it holds afterwards, from the tenant pool.

UserDetailResponse.description:
One user for the user detail screen: as in the list, with when a system admin suspended them, that system admin's name and the reason
(null when the user is not suspended, and the reason null for a suspension before it was asked), the name of the system admin who
granted them system admin (null for a user who is none, for a root's first entry, which the platform grants, and for a grant before
it was kept), and every membership by the tenant's name.

UserListPageResponse.description: A page of the user list (K5), and how many users of the whole list are in each status.

UserMembershipResponse.description:
A tenant the user is a member of: its id, name, slug and status, the user's role there, when they joined, and whether they are
its last Owner. The suspend dialog warns with `lastOwner`, and the delete refusal names those tenants.

UserMembershipResponseTenantStatus.description: The status of a tenant a user is a member of: active, or suspended, closed or purging when its members cannot enter it. A purged tenant has no member.

UserNameResponse.description:
A user's name as it is stored now, resolved on read, as the audit names are (K3). A user a system admin deleted has no name and
`deleted`, and the screen shows "Deleted user". It holds no email address.

UserResponse.description:
A user: our user id, not the identity provider's, their email address and name, their status (active, suspended or
deleted), whether they are a system admin, whether they are a root system admin, whom the configuration names and no system admin
can revoke, when they were granted system admin (null when they are none; a root gets the grant when they first enter the platform),
how many tenants they are a member of, and when they became a user.

UserResponseStatus.description: The status of a user. A system admin deleted a deleted user, and ControlPlane keeps no email address or name of theirs.

UserStatusCountsResponse.description: How many users are in each status, without the search or any filter: the tabs of the Users list.

VerificationCodeResponse.description: A code went out: until when it works.

bearer.description: A session token of the identity provider, in the Authorization header.
